sources.title: RFC 1122 — Internet Host Communication Layers
supports: Link, internet and transport layers as a diagnostic mental model
Layers are logical distinctions, not a guarantee about implementation
notes: Section 1.1.3, Link Layer, Internet Layer and Transport Layer

sources.title: RFC 791 — Internet Protocol
supports: IPv4 datagram addressing, forwarding and routing decisions

sources.title: RFC 9293 — Transmission Control Protocol
supports: Connection synchronization and established TCP data transfer
notes: Section 3.3.2 state machine and Section 3.5 establishing a connection

sources.title: RFC 9110 — HTTP Semantics
supports: POST request semantics, HTTP status codes, origin/intermediary responsibilities
notes: Sections 3, 9.3.3 and 15: HTTP requests and responses are not transport errors

sources.title: RFC 9112 — HTTP/1.1
supports: HTTP/1.1 message framing and connection management over transport
notes: Sections 2.1 and 9; example transport is HTTP/1.1 over TCP, not all HTTP versions

claims.statement: Internet host communication can be analyzed through link, internet and transport layers; the layers are a logical model rather than a requirement for distinct physical modules.
claims.rationale: RFC 1122 explicitly names the layers and cautions that strict implementation layering is imperfect.

claims.statement: IPv4 datagrams carry addressing used for routing across networks; the IP layer does not itself provide a reliable connection.
claims.rationale: RFC 791 defines datagram addressing and how gateways select paths without end-to-end circuits.

claims.statement: TCP establishes connection state before application data transfer, with SYN and ACK synchronization and an ESTABLISHED state.
claims.locator: Section 3.3.2 State Machine Overview; Section 3.5 Establishing a Connection
claims.rationale: RFC 9293 documents the three-way handshake and transfer of data after connection establishment.

claims.statement: A basic HTTP/1.1 request contains a request-line, header section and optional body, sent over a transport connection.
claims.locator: Section 2.1 Message Format; Section 9 Connection Management
claims.rationale: RFC 9112 states the wire format and the expected connection management for HTTP/1.1.

claims.statement: HTTP response status codes communicate an HTTP request result, unlike a connection-refused failure where no HTTP response arrives.
claims.locator: Section 15 Status Codes; Section 3 Message Semantics
claims.rationale: RFC 9110 defines a status code as part of an HTTP response; transport connection refusal cannot carry one.

claims.statement: HTTP interactions can involve intermediaries that forward or interpret requests before they reach the origin server.
claims.rationale: RFC 9110 describes HTTP intermediaries, which provides a grounded L7 proxy/load-balancer example.
